disease_label_per_paper: Human outbreak of trichinellosis caused by Trichinella papuae nematodes, Cambodia
presentation_summary: This case file structures patient 2 from a 2017 Cambodian outbreak caused by Trichinella papuae after consumption of raw wild pig meat.
The outbreak involved 33 infected persons; available hospitalized patients developed trichinellosis after raw wild pig meat eaten during July-August 2017.
Patient 2 was a 31-year-old man with myalgia, fever, headache, edema, and dyspnea.
His hospital stay was 9 days; laboratory table reported leukocytes 23 x10^9/L, eosinophils 4 x10^9/L, neutrophils 18 x10^9/L, CPK 1,216 U/L, LDH 577 U/L, and AST 310 U/L.
Muscle biopsy was positive; the paper table reports PCR pattern negative/positive/not determined for conventional PCR / multiplex PCR / sequencing in this patient.
The article reports that one hospitalized patient died from multiorgan failure probably caused by septicemia after an appendectomy two weeks before death; this corresponds to patient 2 in the table.

Only patient-2-specific table values were encoded as observations. Outbreak-level imaging, treatment, or percentage summaries were not assigned to this patient unless explicitly linked.
